configuration: Native aarch64/x86_64 per ISA original Go TLS/Rust nonprobe five modes; shared Normal/off client128/server64, four TCP bulk+160 UDP/TCP echo, real TUN/raw and owned Stop, explicit MTU1160/no injected netem, original authenticated server native outer repair=0 and client native Stop=0. Per ISA identical binaries first without independent observer and then with 500ms stage+task-stat observer.
method: Exact authenticated Linux Rust RX/TX worker TIDs captured cold once, independent observer samples /proc/self/task/TID/stat utime/stime at USER_HZ=100. 31 samples within true 15.02s app echo window per role. Original background_tun_once returns at most one real send_kernel_multimsg; only copied>0 positive turns count in 5 bins, 0-copy and uncertain not counted.
findings: Client TX worker under real bulk load spends >60% of measured CPU in Linux system mode on both ISAs; server RX similar. Does not attribute to a specific syscall.
Most definite-positive copied client M4 send turns already involve 17-32 records. Larger fixed send batch is not supported by the observed bottleneck.
UDP missing and >1s small TCP p99 on observer leg remain unacceptable.
limits: A->B only, observer adds thread, /proc reads and scheduling overhead; no A' and no causal CPU/goodput or latency interpretation.
Scoped worker Linux system time can include other kernel overhead, not exclusively sendmmsg/recvmmsg.
Only definite-positive copied M4 turns; does not measure all attempted send syscalls, zero copied turns, uncertain or peer delivery.
Different ISA runners not causal comparisons; source-locked binary hashes/per-sample records available in Action artifacts.
No default 1460MTU, WAN/Windows, physical, GE1%, upstream 3s outage, or full timely delivery qualification.
next: Read original native Linux raw send/receive kernel service paths and test a single bounded source-level cost reduction only after isolating dominant system calls; do not increase M4 32 cap or reintroduce UDP priority eviction.
